newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Moscow court postpones Rosgosstrakh sale hearing.
newsitem.headline: Moscow court postpones Rosgosstrakh sale hearing.

text.p: The Moscow Arbitration Court postponed a suit from a union of depositors in Russia's biggest insurer OAO Rosgosstrakh against the State Property Committee until June 23, a Rosgosstrakh official said on Monday.

The union filed a suit against Russia's privatisation ministry, the State Property Committee, due to fears that a privatised Rosgosstrakh would not repay money on policies issued before economic reforms started in 1992.
Deputy chairman Vyacheslav Lemisov told Reuters the suit was postponed as Rosgosstrakh presented documents saying the government had taken responsibility for these policies.

Rosgosstrakh also presented documents saying the union, registered in 1997, did not have the right to sue the State Property Committee which took the decision to privatise Rosgosstrakh in November 1996, he said.

According to the controversial privatisation plan, Rosgosstrakh employees bought 20 percent of shares and a management team has a priority right to buy 30 percent. The remaining 50 percent will be sold at an auction this year.
According to different estimates, Rosgosstrakh owes between 24 and 30 trillion roubles in 1992 prices (up to $300 million at exchange rates early this year.)
